1   The Interim Condensed Financial Statements have been prepared in compliance with Sri Lanka Accounting Standard LKAS 34 - Interim
    Financial Reporting. These Interim Condensed Financial Statements should be read in conjunction with the Annual Financial Statements
    for the year ended 31st March 2025.

    The Interim Condensed Financial Statements have been prepared on a historical cost basis, except for, land, biological assets and financial
    instruments.

    These Statements also provide information required by the Colombo Stock Exchange.

2   There has not been a significant change in the nature of the contingent liabilities, which were disclosed in the Annual Report for the year
    ended 31st March 2025. The presentation and classification of the Financial Statements of the previous year have been amended, where
    relevant, for better presentation and to be comparable with those of the current year.

3   Other than what is mentioned below, no other circumstances have arisen since the reporting date, which would require adjustments to,
    or disclosure in the Financial Statements

    Rights Issue and Subsequent Allotment
    On 21st January 2026 it was resolved to increase the Company’s Stated Capital by way of a Rights Issue amounting to Rs 9,000.0 million.
    Accordingly, the Board approved the issuance of three (3) new Ordinary Voting Shares for every fifty (50) existing ordinary voting shares
    held by the shareholders in the register of shareholders as at end of the date of entitlement at a price of Rs. 200 per share.

    As at 31 March 2026, subscription monies amounting to Rs. 9,000.0 million relating to the rights issue has been recognized by the
    Company, of which Rs. 8,998.8 million was recognized as receivables from shares pending allotment and Rs. 1.2 million as cash at bank.
    The corresponding amount was recognized within equity under Pending Share Allotment.

    The share allotment was completed on 27 April 2026, upon which the balance recognized under Pending Share Allotment was
    transferred to stated capital.

7     DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS AND ASSETS HELD FOR SALE
     As at the reporting date, the Group was committed to dispose of the major operating assets of Luxury Resort (Pvt) Ltd,
     a wholly owned subsidiary of Hayleys PLC, by entering into a binding contract by way of a letter of intent dated 03rd
     February 2026, which comprises the disposal of property, plant and equipment, leasehold rights, intangible assets, and
     inventories relating to its hotel operations in the Maldives. Subsequently, on 16th May 2026, Hayleys PLC entered into
     an asset purchase agreement with the potential buyer, Bohemia Luxury Resort (Pvt) Ltd for a consideration of USD
     17,250,000 and Management expects the transaction to be completed within the first few months from the reporting
     date.

     Accordingly, the respective assets and liabilities directly associated with Luxury Resort (Pvt) Ltd have been classified
     as held for sale, resulting in the subsidiary being presented as a discontinued operation in the consolidated financial
     statements in accordance with SLFRS 5 – Non-current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations.


     The post-tax loss of the discontinued operation has been presented separately in the consolidated statement of profit
     or loss and other comprehensive income. Comparative information in the consolidated statement of profit or loss and
     other comprehensive income has also been restated to present the operation as a discontinued operation in
     accordance with SLFRS 5 – Non-current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations.

 7.3 Losses on impairement of subsidiaries and amounts due from subsidraies recognized in Hayleys PLC

     As a result of the committed disposal of the major operating assets of Luxury Resort (Pvt) Ltd, a wholly owned
     subsidiary of Hayleys PLC for a consideration of USD 17,250,000, management has assessed that there is
     uncertainty over the recoverability of its investment and related receivables as at 31 March 2026. Accordingly,
     Hayleys PLC has recognised an impairment loss of Rs. 6.9 billion in the statement of profit or loss, which includes
     impairment of investments in Luxury Resort (Pvt) Ltd amounting to Rs. 2.9 billion and impairment of balances
     receivable from Luxury Resort (Pvt) Ltd amounting to Rs. 2.5 billion.

9    EARNINGS PER SHARE

    On 21st January 2026 it was resolved to increase the Company’s Stated Capital by way of a Rights Issue
    amounting to Rs 9.0 Bn. Accordingly, the Board approved the issuance of three (3) new Ordinary Voting
    Shares for every fifty (50) existing ordinary voting shares held by the shareholders in the register of
    shareholders as at end of the date of entitlement and the share allotment was completed on 27 April
    2026, upon which the balance recognized under Pending Share Allotment was transferred to stated
    capital.

    In accordance with LKAS/ IAS 33 – Earnings Per Share, comparative earnings per share has been
    adjusted retrospectively to reflect the bonus element inherent in the rights issue. The adjustment factor
    applied was 1.001382, which was calculated based on the theoretical ex-rights price derived from the
    market value of the shares immediately prior to the rights issue.

    As the allotment of shares occurred after the reporting date, the rights shares issued have not been
    included in the weighted average number of shares for the year ended 31 March 2026, except for the
    retrospective adjustment reflecting the bonus element in accordance with LKAS/IAS 33 – Earnings Per
    Share.
